descriptionChirho: In the Qal stem, describes swiftness or speed of movement, confirmed by Arabic أَسْرَعُ (faster) and Korean 빠르다 (be fast).
In the Qal stem, denotes being of little account, lightly esteemed, or treated with contempt, confirmed by Arabic حَقِيرٌ (contemptible) and Swahili kudharauliwa (despised).
In the Qal stem, describes the abating or subsiding of something (e.g., floodwaters), confirmed by Arabic خَفَّتْ (lightened/abated) and Swahili yamepungua (have decreased).
In the Nifal stem, means to be a light or easy matter, a trifling thing, confirmed by Arabic هَيِّنٌ/سَهْلٌ (easy) and Korean 쉽다 (easy) or 하찮은 (trifling).
In the Nifal stem, describes swiftness or lightness of movement, confirmed by Arabic خِفَّةٍ/عَجَلَةٍ (haste/lightness) and Swahili wepesi (swift).
In the Nifal reflexive sense, to make oneself lowly or lightly esteemed, confirmed by Arabic أَحْقَرَ (more contemptible) and Swahili nitajidhalilisha (I will humble myself).
In the Piel intensive stem, the primary meaning of pronouncing a curse upon someone, confirmed uniformly by Arabic لَعَنَ (curse), Korean 저주하다 (curse), and Swahili -laani (curse).
In the Pual passive stem, to be cursed or placed under a curse, confirmed by Arabic يُلْعَنُ/مَلْعُونَةٌ (be cursed) and Swahili -laaniwa (be cursed).
A distinct Piel sense meaning to shake, brandish, or whet, confirmed by Arabic رَجَّ/قِلْقَل (shake/agitate) and Korean 흔들었다/갈았다 (shook/sharpened), semantically distant from cursing.
In the Hifil causative stem, to make lighter or reduce a burden or load, confirmed by Arabic خَفِّفْ/يُخَفِّفُ (lighten) and Swahili punguza (reduce).
In the Hifil causative stem, to treat as light or worthless, to dishonor or despise a person, confirmed by Arabic أَهَانَ/لِيُهِينَ (dishonor) and Swahili kudhalilisha/kudharau (despise).
In the Hitpael reflexive-intensive stem, to shake or tremble, confirmed by Arabic تَتَزَلْزَلُ (tremble/quake) and Swahili vikitikisika (shake).
